lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: permutations and combinations for counting

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: P(A) = 4/10, P(B|A) = 5/10. Find P(A and B).

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A trial succeeds with probability 5/10 and is repeated 2 times independently. Let X count the successes. Find P(X = 0) as a decimal.
From 10 distinct items, how many ways are there to choose 3 and arrange them in order?
A random variable takes values 10, 7, 2, 18 with probabilities 7/10, 1/10, 1/10, 1/10 respectively. Find its expected value.
Given P(A) = 6/10 and P(B | A) = 9/10, find P(A and B) in lowest terms.
A trial succeeds with probability 4/10 and is repeated 2 times independently. Let X count the successes. Find P(X = 0) as a decimal.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: From 6 distinct items, how many ways are there to choose 3 when the order does not matter?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A random variable takes values 13, 11, 5, 14 with probabilities 4/10, 2/10, 1/10, 3/10 respectively. Find its expected value.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Given P(A) = 7/10 and P(B | A) = 7/10, find P(A and B) in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
